consensus_summary: All four blind responses converge on bread primarily symbolizing Jesus Christ himself — the 'Bread of Life' — and his body given in the Eucharist/Lord's Supper (John 6; Matt 26:26; 1 Cor 11), with the manna typology behind it. The 'word of God' sense (Deut 8:3; Matt 4:4) appears in every response but only as a common secondary/alternative meaning, alongside daily provision, fellowship, and leaven-as-corruption.
book_summary: The book identifies bread as 'the word of God,' adding a leaven distinction: unleavened bread is pure doctrine, leavened bread contains corrupting doctrine. It makes no mention of Christ as the Bread of Life or the Eucharistic body.
consensus_core_identification: Bread = Christ himself / his body given for believers (Bread of Life, Eucharistic bread), grounded in John 6 and the Last Supper institution texts.
book_core_identification: Bread = the word of God / doctrine, with leaven-state indicating the purity (unleavened) or corruption (leavened) of that doctrine.
boundary_disagreement: The book's leaven refinement (unleavened = pure doctrine, leavened = corrupting doctrine) partly overlaps the consensus's leaven-as-corruption alternative, but the consensus applies leaven to sin/false teaching generally while the book folds it into a single bread-as-doctrine scheme. The book also excludes the whole Eucharistic/christological range of cases (John 6, Last Supper texts) that the consensus makes central.
material_contradiction: The consensus's central referent is a person — Christ and his sacrificial body — while the book's is a message — the word of God/doctrine. The book presents its identification as the meaning of bread without any common-view note, so accepting it as the core requires displacing the christological/Eucharistic identification that every blind response ranked primary. Although 'word of God' appears in the consensus lists, it appears only as a secondary alternative, not as the central identification, so the book replaces rather than refines the consensus core.
rationale: Both axes point away from MATCH: the book elevates what the consensus treats as a common secondary sense (bread = word of God, Deut 8:3; Matt 4:4) to the sole primary identification, and it omits entirely the reading that all four responses agree is dominant (Christ/Eucharistic body). This is not a boundary adjustment within the same referent-category; it is a substitution of the central referent (doctrine in place of Christ's body), so DIVERGENT is more accurate than REFINED. Extensions partially overlap (word-of-God texts, leaven texts are retained; Eucharistic texts are dropped or reclassified), which fits PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION rather than DIFFERENT_REFERENT outright.
strongest_objection: The book's identification is not alien to the consensus — every blind response lists 'the word of God' as a common alternative meaning, and Matthew 16:12 explicitly equates leaven with doctrine, so one could argue the book merely selects and sharpens an acknowledged strand (REFINED, or even COMPATIBLE_OVERLAP at the core). Additionally, in Johannine theology Christ is the Word, so 'bread = word of God' and 'bread = Christ' could be harmonized rather than opposed. Against this, Deut 8:3 and Matt 4:4 actually contrast bread with the word rather than equating them, and the book's flat, exclusive definition omits the christological center the consensus deems primary.
